subject: Banking
title: Lehman Brothers: The Crash Heard Worldwide
description: One-minute skill: Lehman Brothers: The Crash Heard Worldwide.

hook.text: On September 15, 2008, Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy. $639 billion in assets vanished.

buildup.text: Lehman held massive positions in mortgage-backed securities.

discovery.text: The government decided not to bail out Lehman. Officials believed the market could absorb the failure.

twist.text: The money market fund Reserve Primary broke the buck because of Lehman exposure.

climax.text: Lehman's failure proved that one bankruptcy can crash the world economy.

punchline.text: $639 billion bankruptcy. The world economy nearly collapsed in 48 hours.

quiz.question: What happened when the government let Lehman Brothers fail?
options: Global financial panic spread within hours

details.summary: Lehman Brothers' bankruptcy on September 15, 2008 was the largest in US history at $639 billion, triggering a global financial panic that froze credit markets, crashed stock prices, and pushed the world economy into the Great Recession.
details.whyItMatters: Lehman's failure proved that letting a major interconnected bank collapse can cause a global catastrophe. The resulting crisis cost the global economy tens of trillions of dollars and affected billions of lives.
takeaways: Lehman's $639 billion bankruptcy was the largest in American history
The failure froze global credit markets within hours
The Dow Jones fell 504 points on the day of the bankruptcy filing

faq.question: Why did the government let Lehman Brothers fail?
faq.answer: Political backlash from the Bear Stearns rescue made another bailout politically toxic. Treasury Secretary Paulson and Fed Chair Bernanke have said they lacked legal authority for a rescue, though critics argue they chose not to find a way.

faq.question: What happened to the global economy after Lehman's collapse?
faq.answer: Credit markets froze worldwide, stock markets crashed, trade volumes collapsed, and millions lost jobs. Global GDP contracted for the first time since World War II. The resulting Great Recession lasted years and some economies took a decade to recover.
